audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Volibear five of seven stages (Skill / Volibear x5 / Skill) while six of the seven whys describe Trundle winning that exact stage — "level 1 Volibear loses the sustained auto battle", "he cannot escape the ice zone", "Volibear's auto-reliant kit falls apart inside Frozen Domain at level 3", "Subjugate at 6 converts Volibear's tank stats into yours", "keeping Volibear locked in your Frozen Domain". Trundle wins 52.63% over 190 games.
audit.why: Same failure as the Tryndamere entry: the stage labels were generated separately from the paragraphs under them and point the opposite way. The kit backs the paragraphs — Volibear's only leap is Stormbringer at level 6, so before that he has no way out of a Frozen Domain with a Pillar of Ice behind him.
audit.corrected: Trundle through first item; two-plus items stays Skill, where Stormbringer's team-fight window is real.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and whys[4] treat level 6 as purely Trundle's, and spikes[3] and whys[6] describe Stormbringer's late window, but no field on the page carries the number that decides which of the two ultimates is actually available.
audit.why: Stormbringer is 160/135/110 seconds. Subjugate is 120/100/80. At rank 1 Trundle's ultimate comes back forty seconds sooner than Volibear's, and that gap — not the raw power of either — is why level 6 onward belongs to Trundle in a side lane. A player who knows the numbers plays the second fight; a player who does not respects a leap that is still 90 seconds away.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer 160s at rank 1 against Subjugate's 120s. The fight after he spends it is free.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields attribute Volibear's stun to the wrong ability: wants.foe[0] "Proc his E hand-of-god stun", `early` "Watch for his E stun at level 2", whys[3] "His E stun is dangerous but telegraphed", spikes[3] "respect his E stun before committing", `late` "his team can follow a stun from E".
audit.why: Sky Splitter is the E and it damages, slows and shields him if he stands inside the blast — there is no stun in it. The stun is Thundering Smash, the Q, on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 seconds, and Riot's text is specific about how it lands: he gains speed toward enemies and stuns the first one he ATTACKS. So the tell is the run-up, not a cast animation, and the cooldown a player should be counting is twelve seconds, not sixteen. Baiting the wrong ability is worse than baiting nothing.
audit.corrected: Stun = Thundering Smash (Q), 12s at rank 1, applied by his next attack. Sky Splitter (E, 16s) damages, slows and shields him inside the blast.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields call Thundering Smash a dash: wants.you[2] "block his Q dash escape route", wants.foe[1] "Use Q empowered dash to reposition out of your Pillar slow", `mid` "His Q dash can reposition him out of your pillar", whys[1] "he has W bite but no Q dash yet", whys[5] "unable to Q dash to safety".
audit.why: Thundering Smash grants movement speed toward enemies — it is not a dash and it carries no dash flag in the kit library. Volibear's only leap is Stormbringer at level 6. This matters because it flips the Pillar of Ice verdict: the page keeps warning that his Q will reposition him out of the pillar, when in fact impassable terrain genuinely stops a champion who is only running faster. Before level 6 there is nothing in his kit that crosses it.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash is move speed, not a dash. His only leap is Stormbringer at 6 — Pillar of Ice really does hold him.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], wants.you[0], whys[0] and whys[2] all build the lane around "your AS steal" from Chomp. `mid` also says "use the second cast when his W bite cooldown is up".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage; there is no attack-speed component. Against Volibear the confusion is doubly costly, because The Relentless Storm gives HIM attack speed off attacks and abilities — the stat the page thinks Trundle is stealing is the one Volibear is building. And Subjugate has one cast whose steal doubles over 4 seconds; the "second cast" does not exist.
audit.corrected: Chomp: damage, movement slow, AD sap. Subjugate: one cast, doubling over 4 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frenzied Maul is referred to only as "his W bite" or "W heal" and its actual condition is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: the first cast damages and MARKS the target; casting it again on the same target is what deals bonus damage and heals him. The heal is on the second bite, so stepping out of his 325 range between casts removes the healing half of the ability from the trade. It is a flat 5-second cooldown and it applies on-hit effects, which is also why _missing-interactions.json raises onhit-itemization here: his damage rides attack speed, so armour alone reads the exchange wrong.
audit.corrected: Frenzied Maul (5s, 325 range): the first bite marks, the second bite heals. Break contact between them.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Thundering Smash twice and gives no figure; the content layer names no cooldown at all.
audit.why: Thundering Smash 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, Frenzied Maul flat 5s, Sky Splitter flat 16s, Stormbringer 160/135/110s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s and Pillar of Ice's 21s at rank 1. Between two Thundering Smashes you get three bites, and Sky Splitter at a flat 16 seconds never gets faster no matter how he ranks it.
audit.corrected: Figures added to breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], early, mid and four whys.

audit.why: report[8] already buys Executioner's Calling on first back, which is right for the needs-antiheal flag on Frenzied Maul. Plated Steelcaps is right for an auto-attack kit. The onhit-itemization flag is worth surfacing in prose rather than in the item list, and I put it in wants.you[0].

No suspectNames were raised for this matchup, and the packet defect "never names any of Volibear's abilities" is confirmed against the content layer — it uses letters only, which is how the E-stun error survived. The full layer's "Thundering Smash (Stun)" gloss is accurate; "hand-of-god" in wants.foe[0] is not a League term at all.

edits.before: Volibear wants to W-bite you for the slow and answer back with autos, but that is exactly the trade pattern you win — Q-Chomp the moment he bites, stack the AS steal, and let Frozen Domain do the rest. His level 1 has no dash yet, so he cannot escape once you are inside his body. Watch for his E stun at level 2; he will try to land it before you can plant W, so bait the E cast by walking up aggressively, then punish the cooldown by dropping Frozen Domain and all-in trading.
edits.after: Volibear wants to Frenzied Maul you and answer back with autos, but that is exactly the trade you win — Chomp the moment he bites, sap the AD, and let Frozen Domain do the rest. The heal only arrives on his second Maul against the same target, so the first bite is free damage for you. His stun is Thundering Smash, 12s at rank 1, and it lands on his next attack rather than on the cast — the speed-up toward you is the tell. Bait it, then punish the twelve seconds behind it.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 you maintain dominant pressure — keep trading with Chomp and back off to heal on Frozen Domain, then re-engage. His Q dash can reposition him out of your pillar, so place E slightly ahead of where he is running rather than directly under his feet. At 6 the matchup becomes one-sided: open Subjugate immediately on any all-in, pop the first cast mid-fight so you absorb his armor and MR, and use the second cast when his W bite cooldown is up and he tries to heal back. The stat drain plus your ice-zone sustain makes him unkillable for about three seconds and very killable for the next ten.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 you keep the pressure — trade with Chomp, step back onto Frozen Domain to heal, re-engage. Thundering Smash gives him move speed rather than a dash, so a Pillar of Ice on his path is terrain he has to walk around; place it where he is running, not under his feet. At 6 the matchup tilts hard: open Subjugate on any all-in and it takes 40% of his armour and MR plus a fifth of his max health, healing you the same and doubling over 4 seconds — one cast, no second button. Break the Frenzied Maul mark between his bites and he never collects the heal.

edits.before: Volibear scales into a legitimate tank-diver late, but your Subjugate continues to strip whatever he builds — if he goes armor, you eat it; if he goes health, Chomp's damage scales. edits.after: Volibear scales into a legitimate tank-diver late, but Subjugate strips whatever he builds — 40% of the resists, a fifth of the health bar. At 160 seconds at rank 1 it is the slowest cooldown in the fight, so a dive he spends it on buys you the next two minutes. In 5v5, save Subjugate for him and drop Frozen Domain in the choke; a lane lead plus stolen resists makes you the hardest bruiser on the map.

notes: Two errors here are severe enough to be worth a file-wide sweep. First, Volibear's stun is attributed to Sky Splitter (E) in five separate fields; it is Thundering Smash (Q), and the phrase 'hand-of-god stun' in wants.foe[0] is not a League term. Second, Thundering Smash is called a dash in five fields; it grants movement speed and his only leap is Stormbringer at 6 — which means Pillar of Ice is far stronger in this matchup than the page believes. The 'AS steal' and 'Subjugate second cast' errors also recur here, exactly as in the Urgot and Vladimir entries.
